front.title: Exact Computation Claim Profile for SCITT

abstract.t: This document proposes an application profile for statements about exact computational claims. Each statement binds an artifact digest, a claim, its input domain, a verifier version, and evidence. The statement uses SCITT COSE signing and can carry a transparency receipt. A relying party checks the computational evidence separately from the issuer signature and transparency receipt.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: A computational artifact can have different claims about its behavior. These claims can refer to output uniqueness, witness uniqueness, deterministic execution, or a checked counterexample. A signed claim needs an exact scope and an independent verification procedure. The SCITT architecture in supplies a signed statement and transparency receipt framework.
This document proposes a payload profile. It does not define a new mathematics or claim that a signature proves a computation correct.

section.name: Signed Statement
section.t: An issuer uses the COSE_Sign1 Signed Statement format in . The protected header identifies the issuer and subject through COSE header parameter 15, the CWT Claims header defined by . It also identifies the algorithm, key and payload content type. This initial proposal uses application/cbor for the payload. The payload contains the profile identifier taa.exact-computation-claim.v1.
A transparency service can register the statement and return a receipt under . The receipt attests to registration under that service's policy. It does not attest to mathematical correctness.

section.name: Claim Payload
section.t: The initial map uses integer keys. The artifact digest and evidence digest are SHA-256 values over exact byte streams. The verifier digest identifies the precise checker implementation. The claim includes a predicate identifier, domain, observation contract, verdict and assumptions.

section.name: Claim Semantics
section.t: The certified verdict states that the named checker accepted the declared predicate for the declared domain. The broken verdict identifies evidence of a counterexample. The unknown verdict states that the checker established neither. Output uniqueness requires exact output-set preservation. Witness uniqueness additionally requires witness-fiber preservation or exact witness counting.

ol.li: Parse the COSE_Sign1 envelope and check the protected headers.
Select the issuer trust anchor and verify the COSE signature.
Parse the CBOR payload and require the supported profile version.
Calculate and compare the digest of the exact artifact bytes.
Obtain the specified verifier and compare its digest.
Obtain evidence, compare its digest, and execute the independent checker.
Compare the checker outcome with the declared claim and local trust policy.
Validate SCITT receipts when the local policy requires transparency.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Issuer signatures authenticate statements and do not prove their claims. A checker can have an implementation error or omit an assumption. A relying party must bind the exact source bytes, claim, verifier version and evidence. A receipt establishes transparency service registration and does not establish computational correctness. Key compromise, issuer identity, superseded claims, private inputs and evidence availability require explicit local policy.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This initial proposal requests no IANA registrations. It uses the SCITT media types in .
